page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, operating under the KVM hypervisor. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the processor delivers modest compute performance, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core metrics falling into the bottom 25% tier. Similarly, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores are positioned in the weak tier. However, memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks performs at an average level, reaching 39.75 GB/sec for reads and 36.51 GB/sec for writes. Redis SET operations also demonstrate average performance, processing 5.94 million operations per second, while LLM inference speeds for small 135M models remain in the middle tier.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.se1.2xlarge is its lower CPU compute efficiency, as evidenced by poor single-threaded compression and decompression benchmarks, contrasted against its generous memory allocation. This makes the instance less suitable for CPU-bound tasks, heavy compilation, or complex LLM inference. Instead, its high memory density relative to compute resources provides a qualitatively cost-effective profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand high-frequency processing, such as caching layers, medium-sized databases, and general-purpose memory-buffered data processing.
